A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same budget-feasible procurement work. All 37 pages of each version, including equations, mechanism descriptions, Figure 1, and Appendices A–D, support comparison; content displaced by pagination can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical mechanisms, approximation guarantees, and proofs, with no original empirical studies in the main text or appendices. Corollary 2 numerically optimizes a theoretical bound rather than reporting an experiment.

after.justification: V2 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. The retained numerical optimization of approximation parameters does not constitute experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Mechanisms 1–5 retain their allocation rules, pricing procedures, objectives, and components. The revised impossibility proof does not change the proposed mechanisms.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or application tasks. Crowdsourcing, language-model API access, and federated learning remain motivating examples.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The two newly cited related works are discussed but are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, or training settings. The numerical optimization described for Corollary 2 is unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies are added or removed. Appendix C retains the same theoretical instances establishing tightness of approximation factors.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates. Expectations over costs and randomized prices are mathematical quantities in the proofs.

E6.justification: The reported guarantees remain unchanged, including the 1/(2+sqrt(2)) welfare approximation and 0.2015 utility approximation with parameters approximately 2.39 and 2.13. Appendix C's tightness findings are retained, and neither version contains empirical result entries.

T1.justification: Proposition 1's deterministic-threshold argument is replaced by a Myerson-payment and integral contradiction proof for general monotone allocation functions, repairing missing coverage of randomized allocations. This is a localized proof correction with the same stated impossibility. Lemma 6 also removes the explicit condition p_i <= B while retaining p_i < B/k, both in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and discussion retain the same claims about welfare approximation, prior-free utility impossibility, optimal soft-budget procurement, hard-budget approximation, and generalized objectives. The new proof supports an already stated claim.

C2.justification: Section 3 now explicitly identifies the welfare benchmark as the integral knapsack optimum, clarifying the scope of its guarantee. The explanations of ironing limitations, applicability to additive valuations, and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same runtime bounds, binary search for ex-ante prices, and ironing/discretization descriptions. No implementation, hardware, code, or data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and the bibliography add Berzack et al. (2025) on dynamic rental mechanisms and Berzack et al. (2026) on constrained buyers. The added discussion distinguishes the latter's bidding and spending constraints from hard budget caps; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits, a short related-work addition, a welfare-benchmark clarification, and rewritten proof exposition. The author order and date change, while the section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 31 to page 32 with unchanged curves, labels, and caption. Mechanism boxes and surrounding text shift position, including Mechanism 4 moving from page 32 to page 33. Proposition 1 replaces a two-case presentation with displayed integral equations.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs Proposition 1's unsupported identification of arbitrary monotone allocations with deterministic prices. Its new argument covers randomized allocations and better supports the stated motivation for Bayesian utility maximization. The explicit integral welfare benchmark and added related-work context provide smaller clarity gains. The improvement is focused: the main constructive mechanisms, approximation guarantees, and remaining appendix analyses are preserved.
